hypothesis: Two tmux session names appeared to identify observer processes for the same V58 prospective ledger, which could have invalidated causal research attribution if both processes had written concurrently.
decision: Retain the current prospective epoch. The older tmux pane is dead, one repaired observer process owns the advisory ledger lock, the complete ledger contains one authenticated run ID, and every persisted sequence is contiguous. No live-capital or research-ledger mutation is required.
falsifier: Reopen the incident if more than one process owns or attempts to write the observer ledger, a second run ID appears, a sequence gap or duplicate appears, the checkpoint run identity changes without an explicit new epoch, or the observer lock no longer identifies the active writer.
limitations: The ledger and its checksum continue changing while the observer runs; the recorded hash identifies only this observation boundary.
A contiguous research ledger proves single-writer persistence integrity, not strategy profitability or decision correctness.
Process identifiers are host-local and may change after an explicit restart.
